HEEWON WEBTOON — bold Korean webtoon / manhwa key art, the finish of a top-tier serialised webtoon cover (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader, Nano Machine). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). MEDIUM CLOSE SHOT of ONE character — waist-up or seated — the face large, placed off-centre on a third with breathing room on the side they look toward, from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye or over-the-shoulder), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft nasal bridge, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. INTRODUCING KIM YUSHIN, thirty-seven, Gaya blood and Silla rank, master of the Hwarang yard. Coronation morning in the palace at Seorabeol: he has stayed at the door of the princess's dressing chamber like a guard. MEDIUM CLOSE-UP from the chest up, low three-quarter angle from her seat: he has dropped to one knee on the threshold and presses his right fist flat against his chest armour over his heart, head slightly bowed, eyes lifted past the camera, steady and warm: "Hwarang Kim Yushin. I will serve you to the end." A level, serious bearded face under hard brows, the rare dry half-smile just starting at one corner of the mouth. Framed above the waist: no sword, no hilt and no weapon anywhere in frame. Cold pre-dawn blue light (#2A5FB8) pours through a paper lattice door at his side and rakes across his face, beard, fist and armour plates. Behind him the corridor dissolves into incense smoke and morning haze: red lacquered pillars, a hanging silk curtain, the warm gold bokeh of coronation lanterns. At the near frame edge, out of focus, the crimson silk sleeve of the princess. CHARACTER SHEET (copy this face, hair and clothes exactly): the sheet shows KIM YUSHIN. KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Colour #2A5FB8. DESIGN HOOKS for KIM YUSHIN: a square-built wall of a man: a broad square face and heavy jaw, deep-shadowed single-lidded eyes under flat thick straight brows, a vertical crease cut between the brows, a wide low-bridged nose, the full black beard cut as a solid block, mouth that rarely moves; blue ribbon tails trailing from the topknot. BACKGROUND: the real place and moment of the scene simplified into big graphic shapes — two or three flat value planes, a gradient sky or smoke, a few crisp architectural silhouettes, clean circular bokeh lights; background lines thinner and lighter than the figure so the inked character pops forward. LIGHT: ONE hard key light from the place throws a crisp cast-shadow shape across the face and lays a thin bright rim line along the silhouette; the character's colour lives in that light, never a glow aura or halo. ACTING: big readable manhwa expression and body language carrying the line they are about to say. Face and clothes from the sheet; a new pose, never the sheet's stance. ONLY THIS ONE PERSON is the subject — anyone else is at most a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge, in period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang or Yamato), never European dress. The quoted line is acting direction only: never letter it, no words or sound effects anywhere. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
